ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p342/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p342/r4.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p342/r4.claim: ʿAli reports that Abu Bakr gave all his wealth to God's cause, prompting rebuke from Muslims and blame from disbelievers, after which this verse was revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p342/r4.anchor: عن علي، رضي الله عنه، اجتمع لأبي بكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p342/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p342/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p342/r5.claim: The apparent addressees are people generally, though another view identifies the polytheists; what is given refers to worldly goods and abundance, which are only temporary enjoyment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p342/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p342/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p342/r6.claim: What God has prepared as reward for His friends is better and more lasting than worldly gifts because it does not end.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p342/r6.anchor: وما عند الله: أي من ثوابه وما أعد لأوليائه

ASAD-NOTES:42:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:42:intro/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:42:intro/r3.claim: The title comes from consultation among believers, a basic social principle of their community.
ASAD-NOTES:42:intro/r3.anchor: is derived from the phrase shura baynahum

STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r13.claim: The sūrah contrasts those seeking this world's harvest with those seeking the Hereafter's harvest.
STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r13.anchor: the contrast between those who seek the harvest of this world and those who seek the harvest of the Hereafter (v. 20; cf. vv. 22, 36–39)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p156/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p156/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p156/r4.claim: Verses 44–50 resume verse 36’s contrast between the opponents’ temporary worldly life and the believers’ lasting Hereafter reward; the believers’ traits make the glad tidings immediate for oppressed Muslims and foreshadow their success.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p156/r4.anchor: The succeeding verses relate to the subject raised in verse 36. The discourse in that verse had reached the stage that the life

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p148/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p148/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p148/r3.claim: Worldly wealth and favors are fleeting provisions; what God has in the Hereafter is better and enduring for believers who trust Him, so they should desire that future.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p148/r3.anchor: whatever lies in the Hereafter with God is better then these provisions and also eternal

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p148/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p148/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p148/r4.claim: Trust in God is the true provision for the journey toward the eternal Hereafter; reaching it requires relying on God and leaving whatever obstructs His path.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p148/r4.anchor: for those people who are desirous of the eternal kingdom of the Hereafter, the real provision for their journey is trust in God

JISHUMI:v9p6259/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6259/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6259/r1.claim: What people receive of worldly blessings is temporary enjoyment: it benefits them briefly and then ends.
JISHUMI:v9p6259/r1.anchor: فما أوتيتم أعطيتم من شيء من نعم الدنيا، تنتفعون بها عاجلا فمتاع الحياة الدنيا أي: منافع الدنيا يمتع به أياما ولا يبقى؛ بل ينقطع

JISHUMI:v9p6259/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6259/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6259/r2.claim: What God has prepared as reward for believers is better than worldly pleasures and lasts, whereas worldly pleasures perish.
JISHUMI:v9p6259/r2.anchor: وما عند الله يعني ثوابه، وما أعد للمؤمنين جزاء على طاعته خير وأبقى من ملاذ الدنيا؛ لأنها باقية، وهذه فانية

JISHUMI:v9p6259/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6259/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6259/r3.claim: Another interpretation urges people to work for God: their reward is preserved with Him and is better than what those working for worldly gain receive.
JISHUMI:v9p6259/r3.anchor: وقيل: فاعملوا لله فهو عنده محفوظ لهم يجازيهم بها، وهو خير لهم ممن يعمل للدنيا

JISHUMI:v9p6259/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6259/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6259/r4.claim: Believers entrust their affairs to God, convinced that their provision comes from Him continually.
JISHUMI:v9p6259/r4.anchor: يفوضون أمرهم إليه، معتقدين أنها تجري من جهته إلى آخر الدهر.

NAHHAS:v4p84/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p84/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p84/r12.claim: خير is the predicate of a subject; أبقى is coordinated with خير, and للذين آمنوا is genitive after the lām.
NAHHAS:v4p84/r12.anchor: معطوف على خير ( للذين آمنوا ) خفض باللام

RAZI-FULL:v27p151/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p151/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p151/r1.claim: Worldly gains are low and perishable: calling them enjoyment signals their baseness, while calling them worldly signals their end; reason favors lasting good.
RAZI-FULL:v27p151/r1.anchor: مطالب الدنيا خسيسة منقرضة ، ونبه على خساستها بتسميتها بالممتاع ، ونبه على انقراضها بأن جعلها من الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v27p151/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p151/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p151/r2.claim: The lasting good belongs to believers, as the verse's contrast with those who disbelieve indicates.
RAZI-FULL:v27p151/r2.anchor: أن يكون من المؤمنين بدليل قوله تعالى : { الذين كفروا }

RAZI-FULL:v27p151/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p151/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p151/r3.claim: Those seeking God's lasting reward must rely on His favor; treating obedience as obligating reward means relying on one's own work.
RAZI-FULL:v27p151/r3.anchor: أن يكون من المتوكلين على فضل الله ، بدليل قوله تعالى : { وعلى ربهم يتوكلون }

SAMIN-DURR:42:36/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:42:36/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:42:36/r1.claim: ما is conditional and the second object of أوتيتم; the addressee pronoun is first object and نائب الفاعل, while the second object is fronted because it has clause-initial position.
SAMIN-DURR:42:36/r1.anchor: " ما " شرطية. وهي في محل نصب مفعولا ثانيا ل " أوتيتم "

SAMIN-DURR:42:36/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:42:36/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:42:36/r2.claim: من شيء explains the ambiguous conditional ما.
SAMIN-DURR:42:36/r2.anchor: " من شيء " بيان ل " ما " الشرطية لما فيها من الإبهام.

SAMIN-DURR:42:36/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:42:36/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:42:36/r3.claim: The فاء answers the condition; متاع is predicate of an omitted subject, فهو متاع.
SAMIN-DURR:42:36/r3.anchor: الفاء جواب الشرط، و " متاع " خبر مبتدأ مضمر أي: فهو متاع.

SAMIN-DURR:42:36/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:42:36/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:42:36/r4.claim: ما عند الله is a relative phrase functioning as subject, خير is its predicate, and الذين is governed by أبقى.
SAMIN-DURR:42:36/r4.anchor: " ما " موصولة مبتدأة، و " خير " خبرها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p620/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p620/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p620/r1.claim: He presents Shura as treating unwelcome events as matters God wills and links its passages on affliction, patience, and adversity to the contrast between transient worldly provision and what lasts with God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p620/r1.anchor: سورة الشورى عموماً هي في مستكرهات الأمور أي فيما يشاؤه الله تعالى لا ما يشاؤه الإنسان

ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r1.claim: On one parse, ‘whatever you were given’ is a relative clause with an omitted object pronoun, and its result clause takes fa because the relative has conditional force.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r1.anchor: ودخلت الفاء لتضمنها معنى الشرط وقال أبو حيان

ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan instead parses ‘whatever’ as a conditional, the second object of ‘were given,’ with ‘of anything’ explaining it.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r2.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : هي شرطية مفعول ثان لأوتيتم و ( من شيء ) بيان لها

ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r3.claim: Every worldly provision is only enjoyment during earthly life; God’s reward is better in pure benefit and more enduring because it does not vanish.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r3.anchor: أي فهو متاعها تتمتعون به مدة حياتكم فيها جواب الشرط

ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r4.claim: ‘What is with God’ is relative, but its predicate lacks fa: being better is already understood from being with God, unlike what others possess.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r4.anchor: لأن الظاهر أن ( ما ) فيه موصولة وإنما لم يؤت بالفاء في خبرها

ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r5.claim: ‘For those who believe’ may modify ‘more enduring,’ or its lām may explain who owns the blessing, with an omitted predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r5.anchor: إما متعلق بأبقى أو اللام لبيان من له هذه النعمة فهو خبر مبتدأ محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r6.claim: The believers rely on their Lord alone, not on anyone else.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r7.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r7.claim: Alusi reports from Ali that Abu Bakr gave all his wealth in God’s cause, drawing criticism from Muslims and disbelievers; this verse was then revealed. No grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p45/r7.anchor: وعن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه اجتمع لأبي بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه مال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p197/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p197/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p197/r1.claim: Whatever people receive refers to the adornments of worldly life, which are temporary enjoyment rather than provision for the return to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p197/r1.anchor: فما أوتيتم من شيء} [من رياش الدنيا] (1) ، {فمتاع الحياة الدنيا} ليس من زاد المعاد،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p197/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p197/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p197/r2.claim: What is with God means the reward He has prepared.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p197/r2.anchor: وما عند الله} [من الثواب] (2) ، {خير وأبقى للذين آمنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p197/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p197/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p197/r3.claim: Believers and unbelievers share only brief worldly enjoyment, but in the afterlife God's reward is better for believers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p197/r3.anchor: فيه بيان أن المؤمن والكافر يستويان في أن الدنيا متاع قليل لهما يتمتعان بها

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:35-36/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:35-36/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:35-36/r7.claim: Whatever people receive is enjoyment during worldly life; what is with God is the afterlife's reward.
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:35-36/r7.anchor: فمتع الحيوة الدنيا } تمتعون به مدة حياتكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:35-36/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:35-36/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:35-36/r8.claim: The afterlife's reward is better and more enduring for believers who rely on God because its benefit is pure and lasting.

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:35-36/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:35-36/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:35-36/r9.claim: The first ما is relative but conditional in force: receiving causes worldly enjoyment, hence the answer takes فاء; the second ما differs.
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:35-36/r9.anchor: الأولى موصولة تضمنت معنى الشرط من حيث أن إيتاء ما أوتوا

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:35-36/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:35-36/r10.speaker: علي
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:35-36/r10.claim: Ali reports that Abu Bakr gave all his wealth in charity, a group reproached him, and this verse was revealed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:35-36/r10.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله تعالى عنه: تصدق أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه بماله كله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r1.claim: The preceding signs of rain and the spread of creatures show that worldly blessings are exposed to disappearance and drastic change, which introduces the contrast with enduring good.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r1.anchor: ولما علم أن جميع النعم من الغيث وأثاره

BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r2.claim: All people’s visible blessings are gifts they cannot independently control; humans are weak and helpless, and should serve and obey the powerful God.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r2.anchor: فلو عقلوا لعلموا ولو علموا لعلمموا عمل العبيد

BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r3.claim: The conditional ما is answered by فمتاع; here it means that any blessing given is only a provision of near, lowly worldly life, useful only during one’s lifetime.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r4.claim: What is with God is intrinsically better than purely worldly goods because their benefit ends; it lasts beyond death, when worldly possessions must be taken away.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r4.anchor: أي في نفسه وأشد خيرية من النعم الدنيوية المحضة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r5.claim: The enduring divine reward belongs to those who have realized the reality of faith.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r5.anchor: { للذين آمنوا } أي أوجدوا هذه الحقيقة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r6.claim: Calling God their Lord suits the mention of beneficence: believers have seen that their nurturing and every kindness come from him alone.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r6.anchor: أي الذي لم يروا إحسانا قط إلا منه وحده

BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r7.claim: Reliance means entrusting all affairs to God as one places a load on a capable bearer, without turning to anything else.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r7.anchor: يحملون جميع أمورهم عليه كما يحمل غيرهم متاعه على من يتوسم فيه قوة على الحمل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r8.claim: Exclusive reliance removes hidden association with others, just as faith removes open association.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r8.anchor: لينتفي عنهم بذلك الشرك الخفي كما انتفى بالإيمان الشرك الجلي

BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r9.claim: The preposition على pictures placing one’s burden on God, conveying ease and freedom from worry; the imperfect verb presents reliance as renewed with each new concern.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r9.anchor: والتعبير بأداة الاستعلاء تمثيل للإسناد والتفويض إليه بالحمل عليه لأن الحمل أبين في الراحة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r10.claim: Those who rely on God share worldly blessings without reckoning and receive what suffices their needs, plus lasting righteous deeds that bring the afterlife’s bliss.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p636/r10.anchor: يجعلها على وجه لا حساب عليهم فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p108/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p108/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p108/r6.claim: Verse 36 branches from 42:27's contrast between expanded and restricted provision and follows 42:34's pardon that spared people sea-voyage dangers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p108/r6.anchor: تفريع على جملة { ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا ( الشورى : 27 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p108/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p108/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p108/r7.claim: Worldly provision is transient, including safety at sea; the successful person does not make it a goal but seeks the immense, lasting reward stored for righteous believers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p108/r7.anchor: بأن ما أوتوه من رزق هو عرض زائل ، وأن الخير في الثواب الذي ادخره الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p108/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p108/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p108/r8.claim: The address is to polytheists in continuity with 42:30–31, while its ruling reaches believers by implication; alternatively it addresses the whole community.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p108/r8.anchor: للمشركين جريا على نسق الخطاب السابق في قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p108/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p108/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p108/r9.claim: The first فاء marks consequence; ما is relative with conditional force, and the second فاء introduces its predicate, though the statement is informative rather than conditional.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p108/r9.anchor: لأن المعنى على الإخبار لا على التعليق ، وإنما تضمن معنى الشرط

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p38/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p38/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p38/r10.claim: God diminishes the importance of worldly life and urges people toward the lasting blessings and high rank with Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p38/r10.anchor: ثم وعظ تعالى عباده وحقر عندهم أمر الدنيا وشأنها ورغبهم فيما عنده من نعيمهم والمنزلة الرفيعة لديه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p290/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p290/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p290/r1.claim: Whatever people receive of this world is enjoyment that soon disappears.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p290/r1.anchor: أي ما أعطيتم من الدنيا فهو متاع تتمتعون به ثم يزول سريعا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p290/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p290/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p290/r2.claim: God's reward is better and more enduring for believers, while disbelievers are prepared for punishment in the afterlife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p290/r2.anchor: لا للكافرين لأنه إنما أعد لهم في الآخرة العذاب

BURSEVI:v8p249#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p249#2/r2.claim: A rational person considers the outcome from the outset and takes warning; a Persian maxim advises looking at the end at the beginning.
BURSEVI:v8p249#2/r2.anchor: فالعاقل يرى عاقبة الأمر فيحذر كما قيل (ع) : (درانتهاى كر خوداز ابتدا ببين).

BURSEVI:v8p249#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p249#2/r3.claim: Whatever people receive includes the things they desire and compete over, such as wealth, livelihood, and children.
BURSEVI:v8p249#2/r3.anchor: {من شىء} مما ترغبون أيها الناس وتتنافسون فيه من مال ومعاش وأولاد.

BURSEVI:v8p249#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p249#2/r4.claim: These things are worldly enjoyment and benefit for a short lifetime, after which they pass away and perish.
BURSEVI:v8p249#2/r4.anchor: {فمتاع الحيواة الدنيا} ؛ أي : فهو متاعها ومنفعتها وتتمتعون وتنتفعون به مدة حياتكم القليلة

BURSEVI:v8p249#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p249#2/r5.claim: Mā is relative with a conditional implication because receiving causes worldly enjoyment, so the response takes fa; an implicit subject completes the sentence, and the causal wording encourages gratitude. Alternatively mā is conditional and the given thing is a second object, clarified by min shayʾ.
BURSEVI:v8p249#2/r5.anchor: فما موصولة متضمنة لمعنى الشرط من حيث أن إيتاء ما أوتوا سبب للتمتع به في الحياة الدنيا ، ولذا دخلت الفاء في جوابها.

BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r1.claim: What is with God refers to the reward of the afterlife mentioned just before.
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r1.anchor: {وما عند الله} من ثواب الآخرة أشير إليه آنفا.

BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r2.claim: Khayr describes the reward's essential quality: its benefit is pure; it is the predicate of mā.
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r2.anchor: {خير} : ذاتا لخلوص نفعه وهو خبر ما.

BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r3.claim: Abqā describes its duration: it does not pass away or perish, unlike what people hold.
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r3.anchor: {وأبقى} : زمان حيث لا يزول ولا يفنى بخلاف ما في أيدي الناس.

BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r4.claim: Worldly pleasures are never free of defects and quickly depart; God's promised reward is better and more lasting, and His hidden favors, lofty stations, and gifts surpass what is in both worlds.
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r4.anchor: ومن الشوائب لا تخلو ، وإن اتفق لبعضهم

BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r5.claim: Those who believe are those sincere in faith, and the phrase is attached to abqā.
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r5.anchor: {للذين ءامنوا} : أخلصوا في الإيمان ، وهو متعلق بأبقى.

BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r6.speaker: الحواشي السعدية
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r6.claim: The Saʿdiyya marginalia takes the lām as explanatory, identifying who receives the blessing; Abū al-Layth's commentary likewise introduces it as specifying for whom the reward is.
BURSEVI:v8p249#3/r6.anchor: وفي "الحواشي السعدية" الظاهر أن اللام للبيان ؛ أي : للبيان من له هذه النعمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p210#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p210#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p210#2/r1.claim: Whatever people acquire is only a fleeting worldly enjoyment; they should not be deceived by it, since this lowly, perishing world will inevitably pass away.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p210#2/r1.anchor: أي: مهما حصلتم وجمعتم فلا تغتروا به، فإنما هو متاع الحياة الدنيا، وهي دار دنيئة فانية زائلة لا محالة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p210#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p210#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p210#2/r2.claim: God’s reward is better than worldly life and lasts forever, so people should not choose what perishes over what remains; this is for believers who patiently leave worldly pleasures.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p210#2/r2.anchor: أي: وثواب الله خير من الدنيا، وهو باق سرمدي، فلا تقدموا الفاني على الباقي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p210#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p210#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p210#2/r3.claim: Believers rely on their Lord to help them patiently fulfill obligations and avoid forbidden acts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p210#2/r3.anchor: ليعينهم على الصبر في أداء الواجبات وترك المحرمات

BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r1.claim: Believers reserve reliance for their Lord in every circumstance and entrust no affair to anyone else.
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r1.anchor: خصوا ربهم بالتوكل عليه فيما يعرض لهم من الأمور لا يسندون أمرا إلا إليه

BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r2.claim: Ali reports that Abu Bakr gave away all his wealth and all the Muslims reproached him, after which this passage was revealed.

BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r3.claim: The superior, lasting reward of the afterlife is for those combining faith, reliance, and the virtues named afterward.
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r3.anchor: أن ثواب الآخرة مع كونه خيرا مما في الدنيا وأبقى يحصل لمن اتصف بصفات وجمع بينهما

BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r4.claim: Believers and unbelievers share worldly enjoyment; the Bustan verse pictures earth as a common table for friend and foe.
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r4.anchor: كما قال في "البستان" : أديم زمين سفرة عام اوست برين خوان يغماجه دشمن جه دوست

BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r5.claim: Knowing worldly enjoyment ends and God's reward lasts, a person leaves worldly attachment for the afterlife; that choice is God's gift to whom He wills.
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r5.anchor: فمن عرف فناء متاع الدنيا ، وتيقن أن ما عند الله خير وأبقى. ترك الدنيا واختار العقبى ، وذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء.

BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r6.claim: Harun al-Rashid's sixteen-year-old son chose ascetic worship; a bird obeyed him but not Harun, and the son said his father's worldly attachment shamed him before God's friends.
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r6.anchor: حكي : أنه كان لهارون الرشيد ابن في سن ست عشرة ، فزهد في الدنيا وتجرد واختار العبادة

BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r7.speaker: أبو عامر الواعظ البصري
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r7.claim: Abu Amir says the prince left with only a ring and Quran, earned a dirham and daniq doing Saturday labor in Basra, worked tenfold when hired, and was later found ill in a ruin.
BURSEVI:v8p249#4/r7.anchor: قال أبو عامر الواعظ البصري رحمه الله : استأجرته يوما ، فعمل عمل عشرة

MUQATIL:42:36-39/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:42:36-39/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:42:36-39/r1.claim: Whatever people are given is only a brief enjoyment of worldly life.

MUQATIL:42:36-39/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:42:36-39/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:42:36-39/r2.claim: What is with God is better than worldly provision and more lasting; these people believe and trust in their Lord.
MUQATIL:42:36-39/r2.anchor: وما عند الله خير } مما أوتيتم فى الدنيا، { وأبقى } وأدام { للذين آمنوا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p104#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p104#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p104#6/r1.claim: Whatever you receive is merely the enjoyment of worldly life; God's reward is better and more lasting for believers who trust in Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p104#6/r1.anchor: ﴿ فما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وما عند الله ﴾ من الثواب ﴿ خير وأبقى للذين آمنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v4p104#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p104#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p104#6/r2.claim: The first mā carries conditional force, which brings the fāʾ in its answer; the second mā does not.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p104#6/r2.anchor: ما الاولى ضمنت معنى الشرط فجاءت الفا في جوابها بخلاف الثانية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p104#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p104#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p104#6/r3.claim: The verse was revealed concerning Abū Bakr, who gave away all his wealth and was reproached by people.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p104#6/r3.anchor: نزلت في ابى بكر الصديق رضى الله عنه حين تصدق بجميع ماله فلامه الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:42:36/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:36/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:36/r1.claim: What people receive means worldly wealth and abundance; it is a brief enjoyment that passes away and should not become a ground for boasting. The address is to polytheists.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:36/r1.anchor: يريد من الغنى والسعة في الدنيا. { فمتاع } أي فإنما هو متاع في أيام قليلة تنقضي وتذهب فلا ينبغي أن يتفاخر به

QURTUBI-FULL:42:36/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:36/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:36/r2.claim: What is with God is the reward for obedience, better and more lasting for those who believe, affirm God's oneness and rely on their Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:36/r2.anchor: يريد من الثواب على الطاعة { للذين آمنوا } صدقوا ووحدوا { وعلى ربهم يتوكلون }

QURTUBI-FULL:42:36/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:36/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:36/r3.claim: The verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, who spent all his wealth in obedience to God and was blamed by people; a hadith says he spent eighty thousand.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:36/r3.anchor: نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق حين أنفق جميع ماله في طاعة الله فلامه الناس. وجاء في الحديث أنه: أنفق ثمانين ألفا

STUDYQURAN:42:36/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:36/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:36/r1.claim: What is given in this world is its fleeting delight, described elsewhere as the enjoyment of delusion.
STUDYQURAN:42:36/r1.anchor: Enjoyment of the life of this world indicates the ephemeral delights of this world, which are naught but the enjoyment of delusion

STUDYQURAN:42:36/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:36/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:36/r2.claim: The world's ephemeral delights contrast with the more lasting rewards of the next life; the passage also refers to 28:60 and 29:64.

QUSHAYRI:v3p167/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p167/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p167/r6.claim: Worldly ease is never free of troubles and, when it occurs, quickly passes; God's promised reward is better than the little present.
QUSHAYRI:v3p167/r6.anchor: يعني أن الراحات في الدنيا لا تصفو

TAB-FULL:v20p520#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p520#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p520#2/r3.claim: Whatever people receive of worldly goods, wealth, and children is only an enjoyment in this life, not the Hereafter or what benefits them at their return.
TAB-FULL:v20p520#2/r3.anchor: فما أعطيتم أيها الناس من شيء من رياش الدنيا من المال والبنين، فمتاع الحياة الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v20p520#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p520#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p520#2/r4.claim: What Allah keeps for the obedient and faithful in the Hereafter is better than worldly enjoyment and lasts, since worldly gifts end but Paradise’s bliss does not.
TAB-FULL:v20p520#2/r4.anchor: والذي عند الله لأهل طاعته والإيمان به في الآخرة، خير مما أوتيتموه في الدنيا من متاعها وأبقى

TAB-FULL:v20p520#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p520#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p520#2/r5.claim: The enduring reward is for those who believe in Allah, rely on Him in their affairs, turn to Him in their needs, and trust Him.
TAB-FULL:v20p520#2/r5.anchor: وما عند الله للذين آمنوا به، وعليه يتوكلون في أمورهم، وإليه يقومون في أسبابهم، وبه يثقون

SULAMI:v2p229/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p229/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p229/r1.claim: Some say even one's visible deeds and worship are a lesser gift than worldly blessings such as hearing and sight, so they cannot secure salvation; blessings are not earned by deserving them.
SULAMI:v2p229/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : ما ظهر من أفعالك وطاعاتك اقل نعمة من نعيم الدنيا من سمع وبصر فكيف نرجو بها

TABATABAI:42:36-37/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r2.claim: The verse divides provision into worldly goods shared by believers and unbelievers and afterlife reward for believers, then turns to believers’ qualities and wrongdoers’ fate.
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r2.anchor: تفصيل لما تقدم ذكره من الرزق وتقسيم له

TABATABAI:42:36-37/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r3.claim: The address is to people generally, and ‘whatever you have been given’ includes all blessings and provision they receive.
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r3.anchor: الخطاب للناس على ما يفيده السياق

TABATABAI:42:36-37/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r4.claim: Calling it worldly enjoyment signals its short duration and lack of permanence: people enjoy it only for a few days.
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r4.anchor: وإضافة المتاع إلى الحياة للإشارة إلى انقطاعه

TABATABAI:42:36-37/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r5.claim: What God has is the reward He stored to repay believers.
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r5.anchor: ما ادخره الله ثوابا ليثيب به المؤمنين

TABATABAI:42:36-37/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r6.claim: The lām is possessive and the adverbial phrase is loose; another analysis connects the lām to ‘more lasting,’ but the first is clearer.
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r6.anchor: واللام في { للذين آمنوا } للملك والظرف لغو

TABATABAI:42:36-37/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r7.claim: The reward is better because it is free of pain and distress, and more lasting because it never ends.
TABATABAI:42:36-37/r7.anchor: وكون ما عند الله خيرا لكونه خالصا من الألم والكدر

TABRISI:42:36-38/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:36-38/r1.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم والباقون
TABRISI:42:36-38/r1.claim: Kufans except Asim read the singular “major sin”; the remaining readers use the plural, here and in al-Najm.
TABRISI:42:36-38/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم هنا وفي سورة والنجم كبير الإثم على التوحيد والباقون كبائر الإثم على الجمع

TABRISI:42:36-38/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:36-38/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:42:36-38/r2.claim: The plural is supported by “major sins”; the singular can also denote a collective, as in Qur'anic references to God's blessing and Arabic usage.
TABRISI:42:36-38/r2.anchor: ومن قال كبير فأفرد جاز أن يريد به الجمع

TABRISI:42:36-38/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:36-38/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:42:36-38/r5.claim: Whatever wealth people receive is brief worldly enjoyment; they die, and it may be gone before then.
TABRISI:42:36-38/r5.anchor: فهو متاع الحياة الدنيا تتمتعون به أياما ثم تموتون

TABRISI:42:36-38/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:36-38/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:42:36-38/r6.claim: God's reward and bliss, prepared as recompense for obedience, are better and more lasting than small worldly benefits for believers.
TABRISI:42:36-38/r6.anchor: من الثواب والنعيم وما أعده للجزاء على الطاعة

TABRISI:42:36-38/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:36-38/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:42:36-38/r7.claim: Trust in God means entrusting matters to Him, believing He orders them best, and turning to Him in prayer over whatever befalls.
TABRISI:42:36-38/r7.anchor: والتوكل على الله تفويض الأمور إليه باعتقاد أنها جارية من قبله على أحسن التدبير مع الفزع إليه بالدعاء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:36/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:36/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:36/r1.claim: Whatever worldly possessions people receive are only enjoyment in this life; God's reward is better and more enduring for believers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:36/r1.anchor: فما أوتيتم من شيء } من أثاث الدنيا { فمتاع الحياة الدنيا } يتمتع به في هذه الدار { وما عند الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:36/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:36/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:36/r2.claim: The verse was revealed about Abu Bakr, who gave all his wealth in charity and was blamed by people.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:36/r2.anchor: نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه حين أنفق جميع ماله وتصدق به، فلامه الناس

ELMALILI:42:34-43/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:42:34-43/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:42:34-43/r4.claim: Whatever people receive in this life is only a temporary worldly enjoyment.
ELMALILI:42:34-43/r4.anchor: Bütün bunlardan anlaşılır ki şimdi size verilmiş bulunan şeyler her ne olursa olsun

ELMALILI:42:34-43/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:42:34-43/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:42:34-43/r5.claim: What is with God is better, pure benefit without evil mixed in, and everlasting.
ELMALILI:42:34-43/r5.anchor: hem daha hayırlı hem daha bekālıdır hem şer karışığı olmaksızın hâlis hayr u menfaattir, hem de devamlı ebedîdir

ELMALILI:42:34-43/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:42:34-43/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:42:34-43/r6.claim: This lasting good is for believers who entrust their affairs to their Lord, trust His power, promises, and warnings, perform their duties, and seek His pleasure.
ELMALILI:42:34-43/r6.anchor: ancak O’na tefvîz-i umûr ederler ve O’nun kudretine

ELMALILI:42:34-43/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:42:34-43/r7.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
ELMALILI:42:34-43/r7.claim: Ali relates that Abu Bakr gave away all his wealth and was reproached by some people; this verse was revealed on that occasion.
ELMALILI:42:34-43/r7.anchor: Hazret-i Ali’den rivayet olunur ki Hazret-i Ebû Bekir malının hepsini tasadduk etmiş, birtakım kimseler onu levm eylemişlerdi. Bu âyet o sebeple nâzil oldu.

ELMALILI:42:34-43/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:42:34-43/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:42:34-43/r8.claim: Faith and reliance are two foundational qualities for religion and success in the spirit of both individuals and communities.
ELMALILI:42:34-43/r8.anchor: gerek bir ferdin ve gerek bir cemaatin rûhunda dinin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:36/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:36/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:36/r1.claim: The Qur'an aims to transform the Jahiliyya social order and form an exemplary generation by turning faith into action, with principles for duties to God and relations with others.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:36/r1.anchor: Kur’an, bu âyetlerde, daha Mekke dönemindeyken, imanın aksiyona dönüşmesini istemekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:36/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:36/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:36/r2.claim: People should regard worldly means as gifts rather than products of their own skill, and remember that they are temporary.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:36/r2.anchor: insan bu dünyada sahip olduğu imkânlara kendi hünerinin ürünü olarak bakmamalı, bunların kendisine “verilmiş” olduğunu iyi kavramalı, bunların geçici

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:36/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:36/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:36/r3.claim: What is with God endures; faith and reliance on God are the path to deserving lasting blessings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:36/r3.anchor: kalıcı nimetleri hak etme yolunun da imandan ve Allah’a dayanıp güvenmekten geçtiğini

BURHAN:v1p128/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p128/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p128/r4.claim: The Shura wording begins with fa, unlike the waw in al-Qasas; it is one of the cited examples of substituting one particle for another.
BURHAN:v1p128/r4.anchor: فى القصص ﴿ وما أوتيتم من شيء ﴾ وفى الشورى ﴿ فما أوتيتم ﴾ بالفاء

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r14.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r14.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r14.claim: Al-Qasas mentions adornment because Qarun later appears before his people in it; al-Shura has no comparable worldly scene, so the addition suits the former context.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r14.anchor: وقد ورد ذكر الزينة في القصص لورودها فيما بعد

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r15.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r15.speaker: معترك الأقران
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r15.claim: Ma‘tarak al-aqran likewise connects the added adornment to Qarun’s story, where it makes the verse fit the narrative; al-Shura contains no such worldly episode.
